If you want to align the caption of a table to the left in LaTeX without using the `caption` package, you can redefine the `\caption` command or wrap your caption text in a `\makebox` environment that aligns it to the left. Below is one way to achieve this:

### Code Example:
```latex
\documentclass{article}

\begin{document}

\begin{table}[h!]
\centering

\begin{tabular}{|c|c|}
\hline
Column 1 & Column 2 \\
\hline
Data 1 & Data 2 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}

% Add a left-aligned caption
\vspace{-3pt} % Optional: Adjust the spacing
\makebox[0pt][l]{\caption{This is a left-aligned caption.}}

\end{table}

\end{document}
```

### Explanation:
1. **`\makebox[0pt][l]{...}`**: This creates a box that aligns the text inside (`\caption{...}`) to the left without consuming additional horizontal space.
   - `[0pt]`: Makes the width of the box effectively zero.
   - `[l]`: Aligns the contents of the box to the left.
2. By default, `\caption` aligns the caption in the center when used alone. The trick is to use a `\makebox` wrapper to enforce left alignment.

### Notes:
- You can customize the positioning of the caption text by adjusting the box or adding spacing with `\vspace` or similar commands.
- While this works without the `caption` package, its customization capabilities are limited compared to what the `caption` or `subcaption` packages offer.
